overview: Raymond du Puy was an early master of the Hospital of Saint John and a key organizer of the Knights Hospitaller as a religious and military institution.
His legacy lies in institutional form: hospital care, religious discipline, and armed service became joined in the Hospitaller model.

contentSections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Raymond du Puy was an early master of the Hospital of Saint John and a key organizer of the Knights Hospitaller as a religious and military institution.

contentSections.title: Birth and early life
paragraphs: Raymond’s early life is not well documented, but his leadership emerged in the generation after Gerard and the First Crusade.

contentSections.title: Character and Personality
paragraphs: Raymond du Puy is remembered as the organiser who transformed the Knights Hospitaller from a charitable brotherhood into a military religious order, and the tradition presents him as a capable, disciplined, and far-sighted leader. As the first to hold the title of master after the founder Gerard, he is credited with giving the order its rule, its military character, and its institutional structure, combining the care of the sick with armed service in defence of the crusader states.

Because the sources are largely the order's own institutional memory, the portrait is shaped to honour a formative leader, and individual anecdote is scarce. What the record supports is an effective administrator and organiser whose decisions set the long course of the Hospitallers as both a charitable and a fighting order, defining a model that would endure for centuries.

The honest assessment is that he is remembered through his institutional achievement rather than through a richly documented personality. He is the leader who militarised the Hospital — disciplined, organising, and consequential — a figure whose character survives chiefly in the durable shape he gave to one of the great orders of the crusading age.

contentSections.title: As master of the Hospitallers
paragraphs: Raymond helped give the Hospitallers a rule, identity, and broader role in defending the Latin East while preserving their charitable mission.

contentSections.title: Death
paragraphs: Raymond died around 1160 after shaping the institution that became one of the great military orders.
